title: Not and contradiction
summary: Negation says that a statement leads to falsehood, and contradictory evidence closes any proof goal.

blocks.text:
The negation ¬p says that p leads to falsehood. In the workbench, ¬p means p → ⊥, where ⊥ is falsehood. If p holds and ¬p also holds, the two hypotheses contradict each other.

A contradiction cannot provide a consistent description of a situation. In a proof, evidence of p together with evidence of ¬p closes the current goal. The step Contradiction from h and k. names the evidence in that order: h proves p, and k proves ¬p.

The order in that sentence matters. The first name supplies a proposition; the second supplies its negation. The kernel also understands the definition of negation, so p → ⊥ can play the role of ¬p when the proof term is checked.

Contradiction is different from proving that a particular claim is false. It shows that the hypotheses already available cannot all hold together. From that impossible situation, the kernel accepts any target as proved.

challenge.prompt: Prove that p and its negation lead to falsehood.
challenge.statement: Theorem no_contradiction. For all p, p → ¬p → ⊥.
hints: Assume p, then assume its negation.
Name hp first in the Contradiction step.

challenge.prompt: Write that p and its negation cannot both hold. Negate the whole conjunction.
Here the target is q, which is unrelated to p. Decide whether contradictory hypotheses still close the proof.
challenge.statement: Theorem anything_follows. For all p q, p → ¬p → q.
hints: hp proves p and hn proves its negation.
A contradiction closes the current target, whatever that target is.
